LESSON: THE CLI AND THE BUILDER ASK THE SAME MAP FOR DIFFERENT KEYS, AND ONE MAP CANNOT ANSWER BOTH. The CLI's own reads are keyed by the SERVED NODE and the builder's retirement/dollar read is keyed by the RESOLVED ACCOUNT; on a two-keyspace county those are different strings, so a node-keyed map makes the builder miss every time (it retires the county) and an account-keyed map makes the CLI miss (the node loses situs, ring and geometry). The fix is TWO maps over the SAME row objects, each declaring which key it answers. Found by the pre-registered F1 falsifier, not by review.

A CHECKER THAT DIFFS pin->main CANNOT PASS A PIN THAT IS AHEAD OF MAIN. `check-ldt-pin-staleness.mjs` reports the pin's OWN unmerged changes as divergence, because it diffs the two TREES (its `changedFiles` are `git diff --name-only pin main`), so a factory pin opened as a draft at an LDT PR's head is RED by construction, on top of whatever main has moved by. The dispatch's 'staleness must pass at the new pin' is therefore unsatisfiable before the LDT PR merges; say so and name the commits instead of hunting for a pin value that makes the sentence true. It passes after the re-point to the merge commit, which is when the pin becomes an ancestor of main.

A CONTROL'S ZERO IS A FINDING, NOT A BLANK. The next-bake header always carries all three outcomes including `still retired: 0`; a header that dropped a zero-count outcome would read as 'not measured'. The test that re-derives the header had to reproduce that shape rather than derive only the outcomes that appear in the rows.

A BOM IN A COMMIT-MESSAGE FILE ENDS UP IN THE COMMIT SUBJECT (`P-351` became `P-351`). Write the message with an explicit BOM-less UTF-8 encoder, then verify `git log -1 --pretty=%s` rather than trusting the write.

THE PRE-REGISTERED FALSIFIER EARNED ITS KEEP TWICE IN ONE LANE: it caught the keying trap the fix itself introduced (F1, at the fixture) and it caught the placeholder golden hash (F5, at the assertion). Both would have shipped under 'the tests pass'.
DEAD-END: `psql -c '\d table'` -- META-COMMANDS CANNOT RIDE `-c` (syntax error at or near '\'). Query `information_schema.columns` from a file instead.

A SUPERVISED NODE SCRIPT WHOSE HARNESS SHELL IS KILLED KEEPS RUNNING AND CANNOT RELEASE ITS LEASE. Its stdout pipe is gone, it survives on partial writes, and it is invisible to a `Win32_Process CommandLine -match` filter. Recovery: read `lease-token.txt` and call `heavy-scan-lease check|release --token <token>` directly; do not assume a dead wrapper released anything.

A WRAPPER THAT POLLS FOR THE LEASE DOES NOTHING WHILE ANOTHER HOLDER KEEPS RENEWING, and two wrappers polling the same seat produce one runner and one spectator (the spectator's log will show 'held by <your own seat>').
